I have been farming this 4.1 mu plot in Quzhou County for 30 years, and I know every ridge and low spot. With a university degree, I do not just copy my neighbors blindly — I calculate nutrient balances and track weather patterns on my phone. But my farm is small, only 4.1 mu, so every kilogram of fertilizer and every kilowatt-hour for the well pump is real money coming out of my household budget. Six people live under my roof, and though my son sends wages back from his off-farm job, I still treat each input purchase as a major decision.

For winter wheat, I will plant an improved semi-dwarf variety in mid-October. Last year I applied 16 kg of nitrogen per mu and harvested 530 kg, but the tillers at jointing looked a bit thin to me. This year I will raise nitrogen to 18 kg per mu. I will spread 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as a base before planting, then top-dress with 20 kg of urea at green-up in March and another 5 kg at jointing in April. I will apply 7 kg of phosphorus and 6 kg of potassium per mu, which matches my field’s medium phosphorus and low potassium levels. I will rotary till before sowing to break up the previous maize stubble properly. For water, I will irrigate three times: the winter storage irrigation in November, the green-up irrigation in March, and one at jointing in April. I will skip the grain-filling irrigation unless May is completely dry, because each pumping costs me about 25 to 30 yuan per mu and on 4.1 mu those charges add up fast. I will spray pesticides three times: a broadleaf herbicide in early spring, a fungicide before heading to control powdery mildew, and an insecticide if aphids show up in May. I am targeting 550 kg per mu.

For summer maize, I will sow a hybrid variety immediately after wheat harvest in early June — there is no time to lose. I will use no-tillage direct seeding because I understand it saves soil moisture and fuel, and with the narrow planting window I cannot afford to let the soil dry out. I will put down a base dressing of compound fertilizer in the seed furrow at planting and side-dress 15 kg of urea per mu at the big-flare stage, for a total nitrogen rate of 20 kg per mu. Phosphorus will be 6 kg per mu and potassium 6 kg per mu. I will irrigate twice: once at tasseling and once at grain filling. I will spray pesticide twice, a seedling herbicide and one insecticide at the heart-leaf stage for corn borer. I expect 650 kg per mu if the summer rains cooperate.

I watch what the neighbors do — if Lao Wang on the east side adds an extra bag of urea, I pay attention. But I also adjust based on what I see in my own field. With only 4.1 mu, a bad harvest is a disaster I cannot absorb, so I would rather spend an extra 100 yuan on fertilizer than risk losing even 50 kg of grain. I plan my whole budget as one piece: if fertilizer prices rise, I cut somewhere else, but I will not cut the core nutrient rates below what the crop needs.
